newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts in lacklustre start to short week.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts in lacklustre start to short week.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were little changed on Tuesday in thin business as traders in London returned from their long holiday weekend.
June Brent sat just two cents a barrel down from Friday's $17.97 close at 0939 GMT, while May gas oil was 75 cents a tonne weaker at $164.75.
"It is beginning-of-week blues after our extra day off yesterday," one IPE dealer said. "The volume is very light."
Dealers said they were awaiting the release later on Tuesday of weekly inventory data from the API (American Petroleum Institute) for direction.

GNI research said in a daily report they anticipated a rise in crude inventories of two to three million barrels while gasoline and heating oil stocks should each be around a million barrels up from week-ago levels.

Colder weather in Europe was expected to provide a little support for the markets, too. Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp said in their three to five day outlook that temperatures would be cool in western and central Europe.
"However, considering the likely readings (except the U.K. and Scandinavia which are/will be cold) and the time of year, heating demand is hardly going to soar," GNI said.
Chartists said that the market was still looking bearish because of the June contract's failure last week to break above the key chart gap at $18.77.
The most important support level now lies at $17.61 a barrel, the low of last month's trading range, they added.
News on Monday that Nigeria's Warri refinery had closed because of ethnic clashes was having little immediate effect on Monday morning.
Dealers said they were keeping an eye out for further developments in Nigeria.
Crude oil exports were briefly disrupted at the end of last month when communal feuding resulted in the closure of flow stations near Warri.
"This is obviously a potential problem but in any case there should be no serious disruption to exports, "GNI said.
